title: Repeat Adjustment to the Top-Performer Rate in Seller Performance Standing
content:
**Adjustment.** The top-performer rate is the base rate plus the repeat adjustment: the no-repeat adjustment of 0.1 when no violation type was recorded more than once in the last twelve whole calendar months, the single-repeat adjustment of 0.05 when a type was recorded twice in that period and none more often, and nothing when a type was recorded three or more times.

This adjustment applies to the rate of top-performer relief under Seller Performance Standing. The violation types are counted one by one — listing policy, restricted product, intellectual property, inauthentic complaint, product authenticity and review manipulation — over the last twelve whole calendar months; a violation lies in that period when fewer than twelve whole months have passed from its recording date to the handling date, counted by calendar date. The type recorded most often decides the adjustment.

## Schedule

| Most violations of any one type in the period | Added to the base rate |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 0.1 |
| 2 | 0.05 |
| 3 or more | nothing |

## Worked combinations (hypothetical)

| Base rate | Violations in the period | Adjustment | Top-performer rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | one listing policy, one restricted product | 0.1 | 0.4 |
| 0.2 | two listing policy | 0.05 | 0.25 |
| 0.2 | three listing policy | nothing | 0.2 |
| 0.3 | two intellectual property, two listing policy | 0.05 | 0.35 |
